title: One transformer block
question: How does one block turn token vectors into better token vectors? Press the steps in order.
bigIdea: Attention mixes information between tokens. The MLP changes each token alone. The residual path keeps the input.
note: Part sizes are not to scale. Numbers are from a real run of code/main.py in this lesson.

parts.label: Token 1
parts.explain: The first of six source tokens in the run. Each becomes a vector of 8 numbers.

parts.label: Token 2
parts.explain: Source token two of six.

parts.label: Token 3
parts.explain: Source token three of six.

parts.label: Token 4
parts.explain: Source token four of six.

parts.label: Token 5
parts.explain: Source token five of six.

parts.label: Token 6
parts.explain: Source token six of six. The run reads a six-token source.

parts.label: Embeddings
parts.explain: The embedding table turns each token id into a row of d_model numbers. The run uses d_model = 8.

parts.label: RMSNorm 1
parts.explain: Pre-norm: the block normalises h before the sublayer, not after. The run uses rms_norm with eps 1e-6.

parts.label: Attention housing
parts.explain: Multi-head attention scores pairs of positions and mixes their values. Masked in the decoder.

parts.label: Head 1
parts.explain: The first of 2 heads in the run. Each head works on 4 of the 8 channels.

parts.label: Head 2
parts.explain: The second head. Its scores cover a different slice of each token.

parts.label: Residual rail (x)
parts.explain: The residual path carries x around attention, so the block adds information instead of replacing it.

parts.label: Add x + a
parts.explain: x plus attention of x. The first junction where the residual rail rejoins the main path.

parts.label: RMSNorm 2
parts.explain: A second normalisation before the MLP. Same function, new input.

parts.label: W1 gate
parts.explain: One of the two up-projections of SwiGLU. The run widens 8 channels to a hidden size of 16.

parts.label: W3 gate
parts.explain: The second up-projection. SwiGLU multiplies silu(W1 x) by W3 x elementwise.

parts.label: Gate multiply
parts.explain: silu(W1 x) times W3 x, elementwise. This product is the SwiGLU activation the 2026 stacks use.

parts.label: W2 down
parts.explain: The down-projection shrinks the hidden 16 back to d_model 8, so the result can rejoin the residual stream.

parts.label: Residual rail (h)
parts.explain: The second residual path, carrying x + a around the MLP.

parts.label: Add h + m
parts.explain: h plus MLP of h. After this junction the block is done.

parts.label: Block output
parts.explain: The run prints encoder output shape (6, 8): six tokens, eight channels each, ready for the next block.

steps.title: Tokens in
steps.say: The run feeds 6 source tokens, one sphere each. The embedding turns each id into a vector of 8 numbers, so x has shape (6, 8).

steps.title: Normalise first
steps.say: Pre-norm blocks normalise the input before each sublayer. The run calls rms_norm, which divides by RMS without subtracting the mean.

steps.title: Attention mixes
steps.say: Two heads run in parallel inside the housing, each on 4 of the 8 channels. In the decoder this step is masked, so a token only sees earlier tokens.

steps.title: Add the residual
steps.say: The rail behind carries x around attention. The junction computes x + a, which keeps the input alive for the next sublayer.

steps.title: The MLP widens
steps.say: RMSNorm again, then SwiGLU: two gates of hidden size 16 multiplied elementwise, then W2 shrinks back to 8. The run uses expansion 2.0.

steps.title: Out comes h
steps.say: The second residual junction adds the MLP result, and the run prints encoder output shape (6, 8). Stack this block and the stream repeats.
